description: No dedicated 'štatistika platobného styku' (payment statistics) dataset section exists on the current nbs.sk site. The Payments section (https://nbs.sk/en/payments/) lists only TARGET services, SIPS, SEPA instruments and payment cards — with no statistics subsection — and the Statistics portal root (https://nbs.sk/statisticke-udaje/) likewise has no payment-statistics branch.

result.result_summary: Fetched both the Payments section and the Statistics portal root; neither exposes a card/ATM/POS statistics dataset page. The legacy path www.nbs.sk/sk/statisticke-udaje/platobny-styk returned HTTP 404.

why_it_matters: The cell's headline topics (card counts, POS/ATM terminal counts, card transaction volumes) are compiled by NBS but appear to be disseminated primarily via the ECB payments statistics datasets rather than as standalone NBS downloads. A collector that only crawls nbs.sk will systematically miss these series.

description: No SDMX or documented REST API for NBS's own statistical series was found. OpenStats and the Makroekonomická databáza are interactive JS front ends with download buttons; the only documented contact points are statdata@nbs.sk and makroekonomickadatabaza@nbs.sk.

result.result_summary: Searched in both languages for an NBS SDMX/web-service endpoint; results returned only OpenStats, the macroeconomic database, and third-party SDMX docs (Bundesbank, ECB) — no NBS API documentation.

why_it_matters: Long-term automated collection from NBS will likely require endpoint reverse-engineering or headless-browser export rather than a stable API contract, raising fragility and maintenance cost. The ECB Data Portal API is the stable alternative for NBS-reported payment series.

description: Several candidate URLs were taken from search-result links rather than successful fetches (časové rady vybraných ukazovateľov, financial sector analytical data, supervisory disclosure statistical data, SDDS Plus data categories). They are recorded as hypotheses.

result.result_summary: URLs captured from search engine results; not independently fetched in this pass.

why_it_matters: The deterministic verification pass must confirm these before they are promoted; a 403/timeout on nbs.sk should not be read as dead.

description: NBS has migrated from the www.nbs.sk legacy structure to the current nbs.sk information architecture. Some legacy statistics paths now 404 while the legacy /_img/documents/ file store still serves historical PDFs, and some pages (e.g. TARGET statistics) exist on both trees.

result.result_summary: Observed a 404 on www.nbs.sk/sk/statisticke-udaje/platobny-styk while www.nbs.sk/_img/documents/... PDFs remain reachable via search results.

why_it_matters: URL stability cannot be assumed for a multi-year collector; link-tree diffing and Wayback fallback should be built in from the start.

description: No NBS statistical dataset on cash circulation (hotovostný peňažný obeh — banknotes and coins in circulation, cash withdrawal volumes) was located. Slovak-language search returned only the Banknotes and Coins information section and a commentary article ('Hotovosť neumiera'), not a data page.

result.result_summary: Searched 'štatistika hotovostného peňažného obehu bankovky a mince'; hits were explainer and coin-production pages under nbs.sk/bankovky-a-mince, no time-series dataset.

why_it_matters: Cash usage is an explicit run topic; if NBS does not publish it nationally, ECB banknote/PSD series and the cash-withdrawal side of the card statistics become the substitute path and must be sourced elsewhere.

description: No standalone, separately published NBS payment-systems oversight report (an equivalent of an annual 'Správa o dohľade nad platobnými systémami') was found as its own publication series on nbs.sk.

result.result_summary: Payment-system oversight is described as a standing NBS function on the /platby and /historia/target2-sk-a-sips pages, and oversight outcomes appear to be reported inside the Annual Report's payment-systems chapter rather than in a dedicated report.

why_it_matters: A collector should not wait for a dedicated oversight report; the oversight narrative must be extracted from the annual report and the payments section instead.

description: No Slovak equivalent of a dedicated annual 'cash report' / 'Správa o hotovostnom peňažnom obehu' as a standalone publication series was located.

result.result_summary: Cash-circulation narrative is distributed across annual-report chapters ('emisia bankoviek a mincí', 'hotovostný peňažný obeh'), blog posts such as 'Hotovosť neumiera', and the banknotes-and-coins section.

why_it_matters: Cash-usage intelligence for SK must be assembled from several channels rather than a single serial document; increases collection cost and the risk of missing content.

description: Searches in Slovak did not surface any NBS narrative publication series specifically about ATM (bankomat) networks or POS terminal acceptance infrastructure.

result.result_summary: ATM/POS terms appear only incidentally in consumer-information pages and press releases; no analytical series dedicated to acceptance infrastructure was found at NBS.

why_it_matters: ATM/POS coverage in workstream A4 will likely have to come from the statistics portal (other cell), the Slovak Banking Association, or commercial acquirers rather than from NBS narrative output.

description: Individual item-level inventories for the analytical-comment, quick-comment, data-insight and blog series were not enumerated in this pass; only the series landing pages were established.

result.result_summary: Series URLs are confirmed from the publications hub, but the per-item payment/cash yield of each series is inferred rather than measured.

why_it_matters: Priority scores for those series are provisional; a follow-up item-level crawl is needed before committing collection effort.

description: Several legacy www.nbs.sk and /_img/documents/ PDF paths appeared in search results but were not fetched in this pass.

result.result_summary: Their liveness is unknown; they are recorded as candidates with reduced confidence, not as verified live URLs.

why_it_matters: The deterministic verification pass should treat any 403/timeout on these as bot-defence or migration, not as dead, and should consult the Wayback Machine before dropping them.

description: General web search could not surface individual SK procurement notices or contracts specifically for payment terminals / ATMs — neither via Slovak terms (platobné terminály, bankomaty) nor English (payment terminals, ATM contract notice Slovakia).

result.result_summary: Search engines returned only portal homepages and generic explainers; ÚVO, CRZ and TED notice pages appear to be poorly indexed or only reachable through their own internal search forms.

why_it_matters: Collection for this cell cannot rely on web search. It must go through each register's own query interface, CPV-code filtering, or the bulk XML/API distributions.

description: UVOstat.sk offers a documented API but every request requires an ApiToken header.

result.result_summary: Documentation (GitHub MiroBabic/uvostat_api) states requests without a valid token return 401 Unauthorized.

why_it_matters: The most convenient aggregated view of SK procurement is not immediately machine-accessible; a token request or fallback to raw ÚVO/CRZ scraping is needed.

description: tender.sme.sk (Transparency International Slovensko's open-procurement site) was referenced only indirectly through a 2011-era blog post; no current page was observed.

result.result_summary: No direct confirmation of the site's current state; it may be archived or merged into another TIS product.

why_it_matters: Historical back-series before ~2014 may need to come from web archives rather than a live service.

description: No public procurement or contract-register evidence was found for commercial bank ATM/POS purchases (Slovenská sporiteľňa, VÚB, Tatra banka, ČSOB), as these are private entities outside disclosure obligations.

result.result_summary: Only state-owned or public-law banking entities (NBS, SZRB, Slovenská pošta / Poštová banka linkage) surface in the registers.

why_it_matters: The procurement channel structurally covers only the public-sector share of the SK payments/ATM market; commercial bank fleet data must come from other workstreams.

description: Reporting on the ÚVO open-data XML feed on data.gov.sk/open.slovensko.sk referenced coverage starting with 2014-2015 and gradual backfill; the current completeness and endpoint stability were not confirmed.

result.result_summary: NASES announcement and a slovensko.digital thread describe the dataset, but no current dataset landing page was directly inspected.

why_it_matters: A collector built on the bulk XML may silently miss recent years or newer eForms formats; endpoint must be validated before relying on it.

description: No vendor case study explicitly scoped to a Slovak bank ATM deployment was found on Diebold Nixdorf's or NCR Atleos's public case-study libraries. The closest CEE evidence is the Diebold Nixdorf CSOB case study (end-to-end ATM outsourcing, 99.8% uptime, ~20-year relationship) which does not state whether the Slovak arm is in scope, and the bank99 (Austria) ATM-as-a-Service case.

result.result_summary: Searched in en; only CZ/AT/CEE-level case studies surfaced, no SK-named deployment.

why_it_matters: The core hypothesis of this cell - that OEMs quantify Slovak deployments - is only weakly supported for the two largest ATM OEMs; SK evidence has to come via the channel partner (Printec) and via competition filings instead.

description: No public Printec Slovakia customer/reference page naming individual Slovak banks was located. Printec's SK presence is documented (country page, ex-NCR Slovensko legal identity, NBS register entry, FinStat accounts) but named SK bank references were not found in this pass.

result.result_summary: Searched in sk and en for 'Printec referencie' / 'Printec Slovakia case study'; only self-description and directory listings surfaced.

why_it_matters: The most important SK ATM channel partner does not publish a customer list, so vendor-customer linkage must be inferred from tenders, registers and press rather than read directly.

description: SK business press (Forbes.sk, reprinted by Asseco) reports that Slovak banks deliberately present vendor-built digital innovations as their own and in some cases contractually require suppliers NOT to list them as references.

result.result_summary: Confirmed as an explicitly reported market norm, not merely an observation of missing data.

why_it_matters: This caps the achievable yield of the vendor-reference route and argues for weighting registers, competition filings, tenders and financial statements more heavily than vendor marketing pages.

description: No SK-named customer was found for card-management/switching platform vendors (OpenWay Way4, Tietoevry, Monet+, SIA/Nexi processing). Searches returned only BG/other-CEE references.

result.result_summary: Searched in en with vendor names + Slovakia/Slovensko; no SK hit.

why_it_matters: Card-processing platform ownership in SK (who runs issuing/acquiring switches) remains unmapped from the vendor side; Asseco's card-transaction-processing claim for SLSP/Poštová banka is currently the only supplier-side signal.

description: No formal SK vendor/partner directory for banking technology (e.g. a Slovak Banking Association supplier register or an ITAS-style banking-tech member list) was identified in this pass; the closest functional equivalents are individual integrators' 'referencie' pages and the international trade directories (ATMIA, ATM Marketplace).

result.result_summary: No dedicated SK partner-directory surface located.

why_it_matters: Without a national supplier directory, actor discovery for this cell must proceed vendor-by-vendor, which is slower and more likely to miss smaller processors and integrators.

description: Searched for a Slovak-university (EUBA Bratislava) study specifically on payment habits / cash vs cashless behaviour using local terms (platobné návyky, hotovosť, bezhotovostné platby, výskum).

result.result_summary: Search returned only generic university/faculty and admissions pages; no SK-language institutional study page surfaced in this pass. Relevant academic output was found only via English-language conference/ResearchGate channels.

why_it_matters: SK academic payment-behaviour research likely exists in local repositories (crzp.sk, opac catalogues, faculty publication lists) that general web search does not index well; needs a repository-level search rather than open web.

description: Big Four search in mixed sk/en returned Deloitte SK material only; no KPMG SK, PwC SK or EY SK banking/payments publication surfaced.

result.result_summary: No KPMG/PwC/EY Slovakia banking or payments study identified in this pass — absence of evidence, not evidence of absence.

why_it_matters: These firms almost certainly publish SK financial-services commentary; a site-scoped crawl (kpmg.com/sk, pwc.com/sk, ey.com/sk_sk) is required before concluding they are not sources.

description: Fitch Ratings and S&P Global bank-level SK sector commentary could not be located as free full text; only third-party summaries (fxstreet) of sovereign actions appeared.

result.result_summary: Fitch/S&P SK bank sector reports appear registration-gated; only Moody's rating-action press releases were found in free full form.

why_it_matters: Rating-agency sector metrics are a stated priority for this cell; access route (free registration vs subscription) must be resolved deliberately rather than assumed blocked.

description: No established SK-language term surfaced for 'ATM/POS terminal estate market sizing' as an analyst product; searches on kartové transakcie and platobné terminály returned scheme PR and media rather than analyst output.

result.result_summary: Analytical intermediaries covering SK terminal/acquiring estate appear to publish in English only (GlobalData/Argus/Verisk).

why_it_matters: Means ATM/POS estate intelligence in this cell must be sourced in English or from primary NBS statistics — no local analytical layer to snowball.

description: Targeted queries naming Trend.sk (etrend.sk), Hospodárske noviny (hnonline.sk) and Forbes.sk — the three flagship Slovak business/economic titles — did not surface any of their payment/ATM articles in search results; results were dominated by Statista, TASR and unrelated Czech pages.

result.result_summary: No etrend.sk, hnonline.sk or forbes.sk URLs retrieved in this run; these outlets are presumed live and highly relevant but remain undocumented as candidates because no actual URL was found.

why_it_matters: Trend and HN are where in-depth Slovak banking analysis and bank-by-bank device counts are most likely published; their absence is a search-visibility artefact (hard paywalls suppress indexing), not evidence they lack coverage.

description: No Slovak-language trade publication dedicated specifically to payment acceptance / acquiring / POS-terminal technology (an equivalent of a 'platobné technológie' trade journal) was found. Coverage of POS/acquiring is scattered across general finance portals and IT magazines.

result.result_summary: Searches using 'platobné terminály', 'POS terminál', 'akceptácia platobných kariet' returned generic explainer and vendor pages, not a specialist trade title.

why_it_matters: Means POS/acquiring intelligence in SK media must be assembled from many low-yield outlets rather than one specialist source, raising monitoring cost.

description: Three of the highest-credibility outlets in this cell (Denník N, SME/Index SME, The Slovak Spectator) operate paywalls that restrict full-text access.

result.result_summary: Headlines and ledes are indexable and monitorable; full article bodies containing the bank-supplied figures are not freely accessible.

why_it_matters: The exclusive bank-by-bank ATM/branch numbers this cell exists to capture often sit behind exactly these paywalls; a licensed subscription budget is required.

description: All URLs in this slice were obtained from search-result metadata; no fetch-based liveness confirmation was performed by this agent.

result.result_summary: URLs are recorded as discovered, with confidence scores reflecting search-result evidence only.

why_it_matters: Downstream deterministic verification must confirm reachability; do not treat any entry here as verified.

description: No public annual report or complaint-count statistics were located for Inštitút ARS SBA in this pass; only procedural pages and forms were surfaced.

result.result_summary: ARS SBA site sections found (o inštitúte, formuláre a dokumenty) but no statistics/výročná správa page confirmed.

why_it_matters: Complaint counts by product are the core value of this body for weak-signal work; if never published, the source must be downgraded or handled via direct request.

description: No standalone SK-only payments/cards conference with a published archived agenda was confirmed; payments content appears embedded in general events (Finweek, ITAPA, New Retail Summit, FinTech Roadmap CZ-SK).

result.result_summary: Searches in sk returned general tech/finance conferences rather than a dedicated payment-systems congress.

why_it_matters: Conference decks are often the only public venue for national payment volumes; absence of a dedicated venue means coverage must be spread across several general events.

description: The canonical websites of Zväz obchodu SR and Slovenská aliancia moderného obchodu (SAMO) were not directly confirmed; their content was reached only via news portals and conference credits.

result.result_summary: biznis.sk hosted Zväz obchodu SR news; samosr.sk is inferred, not verified.

why_it_matters: Merchant-association positions on interchange and cash acceptance are a named requirement of this cell; without the primary domains, collection is second-hand.

description: No HORECA/hospitality-association source with quantified card-fee or cash-handling positions was found, despite the sector being a heavy cash user.

result.result_summary: Only a generic HORECA conference mention appeared in search summaries, with no payments data.

why_it_matters: Hospitality is a key cash-acceptance constituency; missing it leaves a merchant-side blind spot.

description: WebFetch could not reach web.archive.org at all: the CDX query for nbs.sk/sk/statisticke-udaje* returned 'Claude Code is unable to fetch from web.archive.org'.

result.result_summary: No Wayback captures could be enumerated or inspected during this run. This is an agent-side egress restriction, NOT evidence that the archive or the captures are unavailable.

why_it_matters: The Wayback Machine is the load-bearing surface for this coverage cell (retired NBS statistics pages, pre-redesign PDF links). The deterministic collector must exercise the CDX API from an unrestricted environment before any conclusion is drawn about historical coverage depth.

description: No public SDMX or REST endpoint for NBS statistics was found. The OpenStats page documents interactive filtering and download but states no API; NBS procurement documents describe an Open Data solution 'with the use of API' but no live endpoint URL surfaced.

result.result_summary: NBS machine-readable access appears to be file-download and dashboard-export only at present; SDMX for SK payment aggregates is available only via the ECB, not NBS directly.

why_it_matters: Ingestion plans must not assume an NBS SDMX endpoint. The ECB Data Portal is the practical SDMX route for SK payment/card series, with NBS files as the national-detail supplement. Worth an explicit enquiry to statdata@nbs.sk.

description: archiv.nbs.sk was hypothesised to host the retired pre-redesign NBS website. Fetching the site showed it is exclusively the institutional/physical archive (archival fonds, library, researcher portal) with no statistics sections.

result.result_summary: archiv.nbs.sk is not a mirror of the old NBS web statistics; it is a records archive under act 395/2002.

why_it_matters: Prevents wasted crawling effort and mis-scoped expectations; the retired-page problem must be solved via Wayback plus legacy www.nbs.sk paths, not via archiv.nbs.sk.

description: Slovakia is not a member jurisdiction of the CPMI, so the BIS Red Book / data.bis.org CPMI tables do not carry Slovak country data despite one search summary implying otherwise.

result.result_summary: BIS CPMI is a comparator and methodology source for SK, not a data source.

why_it_matters: Avoids a fabricated data path; the CPMI methodology document (d168) remains useful for definitional alignment when reconciling SK series across ECB, IMF and NBS.

description: No specific payments/cards dataset published by NBS on data.gov.sk could be identified by name in this run; NBS is listed among catalogue organisations but the concrete dataset inventory was not enumerated (the organisation-scoped dataset listing was not fetched).

result.result_summary: NBS presence in the national catalogue is confirmed at organisation level only; dataset-level coverage remains unverified.

why_it_matters: The catalogue may hold either rich or near-empty NBS coverage; this determines whether data.gov.sk is a primary ingestion route or merely a discovery pointer. It should be resolved by a direct DCAT/SPARQL enumeration in the collection pass.

description: No dedicated Slovak academic research-data repository (a Zenodo-style institutional data archive holding payment/banking microdata) was identified. Searches in Slovak surfaced only CRZP (theses) and CVTI SR library infrastructure.

result.result_summary: Academic data-repository coverage for SK payments appears thin; theses are the realistic academic long-tail surface.

why_it_matters: Expectations for academic replication datasets on Slovak card/ATM usage should be low; effort is better spent on ECB/IMF machine-readable series and NBS PDF vintages.

description: The ECB Consumer Expectations Survey (CES) covers ~19,000 consumers in 11 euro area countries (BE, DE, IE, GR, ES, FR, IT, NL, AT, PT, FI). Slovakia is not among them.

result.result_summary: CES payment-preference and digital-payment modules cannot be used for Slovakia country estimates; SPACE remains the only harmonised ECB consumer-level source with SK coverage.

why_it_matters: Avoids a wasted collection pipeline and prevents mistaking euro-area CES aggregates for SK-representative figures.

description: Slovak-language searching of ECB statistical content returned almost nothing on payment/card/ATM statistics: ecb.europa.eu serves only general institutional pages (ECB/ESCB overview, euro overview, banknote circulation) in Slovak.

result.result_summary: No .sk-language ECB payment-statistics dataset page, SPACE report, or fraud report was found. The Slovak-language layer for this cell is effectively NBS relaying ECB output, plus EUR-Lex Slovak legal texts.

why_it_matters: Confirms the cell must be collected in English; local-language monitoring should be pointed at nbs.sk and EUR-Lex SK rather than at the ECB site.

description: No ECB-published, Slovakia-specific standalone SPACE country annex (a separate SK-only PDF) was located via search; SK appears as rows/columns inside the euro-area report and its annexes.

result.result_summary: Slovakia coverage in SPACE is confirmed at country-row level (e.g. 42% cash for P2P), but as part of pooled annex tables rather than a dedicated national report.

why_it_matters: Collection must be table-extraction from the euro-area annexes; do not budget for a per-country document feed.

description: The ECB payments-statistics press-release index URL and the ECB Data Portal API help URL were inferred from related result URLs rather than returned directly by search, and no page was fetched to confirm them.

result.result_summary: Individual release URLs (pis2024h1, pis2024h2, pis2025h1) and help pages (getting-data-web-services-sdmx, useful-tips, downloading-data) did appear in results; the index/API-root paths are my inference.

why_it_matters: Downstream verification should resolve these two roots before wiring them into a scheduler.

description: ECB payment statistics moved from annual (ECB/2013/43) to semi-annual with a much wider variable set (ECB/2020/59), and the old annual dataset is explicitly labelled 'discontinued'.

result.result_summary: Two distinct SK datasets exist with a methodological break around 2021/2022; naive concatenation will create false trend jumps in terminal and card counts.

why_it_matters: Any long-run SK ATM/POS or card series must document and flag the break rather than silently splice.

description: Slovakia is not a CPMI member jurisdiction. The CPMI membership list (Argentina, Australia, Belgium, Brazil, Canada, China, ECB, France, Germany, Hong Kong SAR, India, Indonesia, Italy, Japan, Korea, Mexico, Netherlands, Russia, Saudi Arabia, Singapore, South Africa, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, Turkey, UK, US) does not include SK.

result.result_summary: No dedicated Slovakia country table or Red Book chapter exists; SK is subsumed in the 'euro area' aggregate.

why_it_matters: The cell brief assumed 'BIS CPMI Red Book Slovakia rows' exist. They do not as a national series — SK-specific payment/ATM/POS statistics must come from ECB Payments Statistics or NBS, with BIS used only as a euro-area comparator. This prevents wasted collection effort and a false-provenance risk.

description: Searching in Slovak for BIS payment statistics ('BIS štatistika platobných systémov Slovensko') and for Findex ('Svetová banka Findex') returned no Slovak-language BIS or World Bank Findex pages; results redirected to NBS, MF SR and Slovak media coverage, which belong to other coverage cells.

result.result_summary: BIS and World Bank publish essentially no Slovak-language surface for these datasets; data.europa.eu and Eurostat Statistics Explained are the only aggregators in this cell with genuine Slovak-language pages.

why_it_matters: Local-language monitoring for this cell should be pointed at data.europa.eu/sk and Eurostat /sk explainer pages only; expecting sk-language releases from BIS/World Bank would create a permanent false gap in the monitoring plan.

description: Published Global Findex 2025 country outputs surfaced in search were global/aggregate; no ready-made Slovakia country factsheet page was located in this pass, only the global download-data page and the microdata catalogue entry.

result.result_summary: SK Findex values appear extractable only by filtering the global indicator file or the microdata, not from a dedicated SK landing page.

why_it_matters: Collection design must budget for file-level filtering rather than a per-country scrape, and the microdata route may require registration.

description: The 'EU Payment Observatory' is a DG GROW late-payment (B2B commercial payment behaviour) instrument, not a DG FISMA retail-payments statistics observatory as the cell brief's phrasing might suggest.

result.result_summary: Its indicators cover payment terms/delays, not card volumes, ATM/POS estates or cash usage.

why_it_matters: Prevents mis-tagging the Observatory as a retail card-statistics source and setting wrong expectations for what SK data it yields.

description: No eKasa dataset was found that splits recorded turnover or receipts by tender type (hotovosť vs. platobná karta / bezhotovostne). The ODFS eKasa category exposes turnover and receipt counts by period, region and SK NACE2, plus register counts — but not payment method.

result.result_summary: 10 eKasa datasets enumerated on the ODFS category page; none of the titles or descriptions references payment method, card, or cash tender split.

why_it_matters: This is the cell's headline hypothesis — eKasa as the hard cash-vs-card-at-the-till evidence source. The transactional data exists inside the system (receipts carry the payment method) but is not published, so cash share must be inferred indirectly (eKasa turnover as denominator against NBS card-acquiring volumes) or requested via an infožiadosť under the freedom-of-information act.

description: No ATM-related statistics were found from any institution in this cell (ŠÚ SR, MF SR, Finančná správa, NKÚ). Searches on cash/ATM terms returned only central-bank-adjacent or commercial material.

result.result_summary: Zero candidates for ATM network, ATM withdrawal volumes or cash-in-transit from fiscal/statistical bodies.

why_it_matters: Confirms that ATM data for SK is genuinely NBS/ECB territory and that this cell should not be relied on for it; workstream coverage of ATM statistics must come from the central-bank cell.

description: SLOVSTAT, named in the cell definition, is retired: ŠÚ SR suspended its data updates from 1 November 2017 and closed access on 31 October 2018; content moved to DATAcube, which is itself now being migrated to STATdata (created 2024).

result.result_summary: SLOVSTAT confirmed as a dead database in ŠÚ SR's own portal documentation; DATAcube and STATdata are the live systems.

why_it_matters: Any collection design or historical citation pointing at SLOVSTAT will fail; and a DATAcube-only pipeline will silently miss new cubes created only in STATdata during the migration.

description: The canonical hostname and entry URL for the new STATdata public database was not resolved in this pass; searches returned the ŠÚ SR Databázy hub, an older 'STATdat.' page, and PDF exports, but no confirmed statdata.statistics.sk landing page.

result.result_summary: STATdata's existence and role confirmed from ŠÚ SR documentation; its direct URL not confirmed.

why_it_matters: The successor system to DATAcube is the long-term collection target for this cell; leaving its endpoint unresolved is a live risk to pipeline continuity.

description: No specific completed NKÚ audit report dedicated to eKasa or to the Financial Administration's cash-register supervision was located; searches surfaced the ongoing-audits register and the annual budget opinion, but media results dominated over NKÚ's own documents.

result.result_summary: NKÚ audit register and homepage identified as the correct entry points; a targeted eKasa audit report was not confirmed to exist.

why_it_matters: The cell rationale assumes audit-body commentary on eKasa. That commentary may not exist yet; the register should be monitored rather than assumed as a supply of reports.

description: No English-language equivalents were found for the eKasa datasets beyond a partially translated ODFS interface; the substantive fiscal material (IFP analyses, NKÚ documents, dôvodové správy) is Slovak-only.

result.result_summary: English search variants returned the ŠÚ SR English API help page and an ODFS English category path, nothing else of substance.

why_it_matters: Any downstream collection or analysis of this cell must handle Slovak text and Slovak fiscal terminology; an English-only pipeline would capture almost nothing from the fiscal actors.

description: No dedicated Slovak ATM-network or ATM-operator association was found (no SK equivalent of an 'asociácia prevádzkovateľov bankomatov'). Searched with local terms bankomaty, sieť bankomatov, prevádzkovatelia bankomatov alongside association terms.

result.result_summary: ATM fleet totals appear only inside the SBA/NBS monthly card statistics and press releases, not from a standalone ATM body.

why_it_matters: ATM estate tracking for SK must lean on the SBA card statistics XLSX and NBS payment statistics rather than a sector body; no independent cross-check exists at association level.

description: Slovakia has no privately-owned domestic ACH/clearing house: SIPS was operated by NBS and, since euro adoption in 2009, interbank traffic moved to TARGET2 (now TARGET services / TIPS for instant payments).

result.result_summary: The 'clearing operator' actor in this cell collapses into the central bank plus Eurosystem infrastructure.

why_it_matters: Throughput/volume data must be sourced from NBS payment-system pages, NBS annual report 'platobný styk' chapters and ECB/TIPS statistics, not from a national scheme operator website.

description: No evidence found of a surviving Slovak domestic card scheme body (no national debit scheme comparable to e.g. Bancomat/BankAxept). Card issuing/acceptance in SK runs on international schemes with processing via bank-owned/group processors such as Regional Card Processing Centre.

result.result_summary: Scheme-level card volumes are not published by any SK national scheme body.

why_it_matters: Card statistics depend entirely on the SBA/NBS aggregation; there is no scheme-side redundancy.

description: CRIF Slovak Credit Bureau (crif.sk) and Centrálny depozitár cenných papierov SR (cdcp.sk) homepage URLs were inferred from entity names and search context, not fetched in this pass. EPC SEPA scheme-register download URL likewise not resolved.

result.result_summary: Three candidate URLs carry lower confidence and need the deterministic liveness pass.

why_it_matters: Prevents false confidence in URLs that were never opened; none should be treated as verified.

description: The 'Národný plán zavedenia okamžitých platieb v SR' PDF sits on the legacy www.nbs.sk/_img/... path while NBS has migrated to a new CMS at nbs.sk. The legacy link may 404 or redirect.

result.result_summary: Recorded as unverified rather than dead; a 404 here would mean 'moved', not 'gone'.

why_it_matters: Archiving the PDF now protects a key scheme-governance artefact against CMS migration loss.

description: Both credit-register bodies (SBCB/SRBI, NBCB/NRKI) expose only marketing and client-service pages publicly; the register content itself is member-only and consists of personal data under GDPR.

result.result_summary: Only membership and about pages are collectable.

why_it_matters: Sets a hard boundary: no register querying or scraping of client data, only structural intelligence about who participates.

description: No Slovak commercial bank in this cell was found to publish a standing, machine-readable 'card / ATM / POS KPI' page. Searches in Slovak for per-bank card and terminal counts returned annual-report PDFs, fee schedules and press items, never a structured KPI dashboard or open dataset.

result.result_summary: Card/ATM/POS micro-data exists only as prose or tables inside PDFs and press releases; no API, CSV or XBRL tagging of these operational metrics.

why_it_matters: Collection must be PDF/HTML text-extraction based with per-bank templates; expect irregular metric definitions and discontinued series across years.

description: mBank S.A., pobočka zahraničnej banky and UniCredit Bank Czech Republic and Slovakia, a.s., pobočka zahraničnej banky operate as branches of foreign banks and were not found to publish a Slovakia-only annual report with SK card/ATM/POS figures; UniCredit's Slovak-language reports cover the combined Czech+Slovak entity.

result.result_summary: SK-specific volumes for these two players must be inferred from press statements, branch filings in the Register účtovných závierok, or parent-group segment notes.

why_it_matters: Bank-by-bank decomposition of Slovak national totals will have a structural gap for foreign-bank branches unless a proxy method is agreed.

description: Automated fetch of the Tatra banka annual-report hub returned HTTP 403, and one guessed SLSP financial-indicators path returned HTTP 404 (the site appears reorganised toward /informacie-o-banke/investori/financne-ukazovatele).

result.result_summary: Both are hypotheses of bot defence and URL migration, not evidence the pages are dead; the underlying PDFs surfaced normally in search.

why_it_matters: The collector needs browser-like headers or a headless browser for tatrabanka.sk, and must resolve SLSP document URLs from the live index rather than hardcoding paths.

description: Slovak-language searching produced heavy noise from same-named or similarly-named entities: 'Prvá stavebná sporiteľňa (PSS)' returned for 'Slovenská sporiteľňa', 'Slovenská správa ciest' returned for ČSOB queries, and 'OZ PRIMA' for Prima banka.

result.result_summary: Ambiguous local terms identified and flagged as noisy: 'sporiteľňa', 'prima', 'výročná správa 2024' alone.

why_it_matters: Query templates must pin the full legal entity name and site: filter, or the corpus will silently ingest unrelated organisations' reports.

description: No separate Slovak bank entity 'Raiffeisen' with its own disclosures was found for this cell: in Slovakia Raiffeisen operates as a retail brand of Tatra banka, a.s. (RBI group). Searches for standalone Raiffeisen SK annual reports returned no independent SK bank report.

result.result_summary: Raiffeisen SK data is expected to be consolidated inside Tatra banka's reporting and RBI group segment reporting.

why_it_matters: Prevents double-counting Raiffeisen and Tatra banka as two banks when building bank shares of the national card/ATM base.

description: No SK acquirer or PSP was found publishing a regular, structured statistical release of its own transaction volumes, merchant counts or average ticket. Disclosures are one-off marketing claims embedded in prose (e.g. SKPAY '28,000+ POS terminals', Global Payments '37,000+ terminals in Slovakia', Comgate '21,000+ merchants', GoPay '7,000+ merchants', Besteron '1,500+ e-shops').

result.result_summary: Merchant/terminal figures exist only as scattered, undated marketing sentences; no acquirer-published time series.

why_it_matters: Any acquirer-level time series for SK must be reconstructed by snapshotting corporate pages over time and by text-mining statutory annual reports — it cannot be pulled from a publisher-maintained dataset.

description: Searched in Slovak for softPOS merchant adoption numbers (softPOS Slovensko, platobný terminál v mobile, počet obchodníkov). Found that SLSP, ČSOB, Tatra banka and VÚB all offer phone-as-terminal products, and general aggregates (mobile payments = 22% of card transactions; cashless = 55% of transactions; 16 terminals per 1,000 inhabitants vs EU 32), but no provider-level softPOS merchant counts.

result.result_summary: SoftPOS adoption in SK is documented qualitatively and by bank product launches, not by published merchant counts.

why_it_matters: SoftPOS is the main mechanism closing SK's terminal-density gap; without provider-level counts, coverage growth can only be inferred from SBA/ZBK aggregate acceptance-point statistics.

description: The Slovenská FinTech asociácia member list could not be located in search results; only the association's homepage, Facebook page and FinStat/Transparex entity records surfaced. A second association (FINAS) exists but its membership was likewise not visible from search snippets.

result.result_summary: No public membership directory confirmed for either SK fintech association.

why_it_matters: Association memberships are the cheapest way to enumerate small non-bank payment actors; if they are not public, the actor map must lean entirely on the NBS PSD2 register plus press snowballing.

description: No settled Slovak-language term was found for 'acquirer' as an institution type. SK material uses circumlocutions — 'akceptácia platobných kariet', 'prijímanie platobných kariet', 'poskytovateľ platobných terminálov', 'zúčtovacia banka' — while English 'acquiring' appears mainly in EN-language corporate material.

result.result_summary: Acquiring is described functionally, not named, in Slovak sources.

why_it_matters: Query design must use the functional Slovak phrases rather than a literal translation of 'acquirer', or local sources will be systematically missed.

description: The brand 'TrustPay' returns heavy SEO spam from gambling/betting affiliate sites (e.g. trustpaystavky.com) that impersonate payment-provider guides. Similarly 'platobná brána' returns mostly affiliate comparison blogs rather than provider primary sources.

result.result_summary: Two core query terms are polluted by affiliate content.

why_it_matters: Automated collection on these terms will ingest low-credibility affiliate pages; domain allowlisting to provider and register domains is required.

description: Two URLs in the candidate list were inferred rather than observed in search results: the NBS PSD2 JSON endpoint https://subjekty.nbs.sk/api/psd2 (reported in a search summary, not fetched by me) and https://www.besteron.sk/ (constructed from the brand name). Both are hypotheses pending the deterministic liveness pass.

result.result_summary: Two URLs unconfirmed; not fabricated facts but unverified addresses.

why_it_matters: The PSD2 JSON endpoint is the single highest-leverage automation target in this cell; if it does not exist in that form, the HTML register must be parsed instead.

description: No Slovakia-specific Mastercard newsroom section or SK-language Mastercard press page surfaced; SK Mastercard survey findings appear only via Slovak media/PR-service mirrors and the regional (Europe/EEMEA) newsroom.

result.result_summary: Searches in en and sk returned regional Mastercard newsrooms and SK media reprints, no mastercard.com/sk newsroom.

why_it_matters: Collection for Mastercard SK must rely on media mirrors, which risks losing methodology notes and full data tables present in the original release.

description: No published NBS list of licensed money processors / cash-handling entities ('spracovatelia peňazí') was located, despite Loomis referencing an NBS licence for authenticity checking.

result.result_summary: sk-language search of NBS registers returned consumer-credit, crypto and intermediary registers only.

why_it_matters: Without this register the population of SK cash-cycle operators cannot be enumerated authoritatively; the actor map stays media/company-site driven.

description: Brink's presence in Slovakia was not confirmed; searches surfaced only Brink's Czech Republic entities. Likewise no SK-specific 'Cash&Go'/'SEC-Cash' operator was verified.

result.result_summary: sk/cz query returned brinks.cz and CZ registry entries only.

why_it_matters: The SK CIT market may be effectively single-vendor (Loomis SK) plus bank in-house operations — a structural fact worth confirming, not assuming.

description: Apple and Google publish no Slovakia-level wallet adoption or transaction data; only bank-by-bank availability announcements and third-party trackers exist.

result.result_summary: sk search returned bank/media launch coverage and an availability overview, no vendor statistics.

why_it_matters: Wallet penetration for SK must be inferred from scheme surveys (e.g. Mastercard's 56% mobile-payment figure) and issuer disclosures, not from the wallet providers.

description: No URL in this slice was fetched; all entries come from search-result metadata and snippets. Several (visa.sk deep press-release URL, ebankomaty.sk, bitcoinmat.org) are plausible but unverified and may redirect or have moved.

result.result_summary: Search-only discovery pass.

why_it_matters: The deterministic verification pass should treat these as hypotheses; 403s from corporate CDNs (visa.sk, mastercard.com) are expected and do not mean dead.

description: No separate, standalone public NBS register of payment-service AGENTS (agenti platobných služieb) or distributors of e-money was located as its own page; agent records appear to be embedded inside the PSD2 register/subjekty database rather than published as a distinct list.

result.result_summary: Searches in sk for 'register agentov platobných služieb' surfaced only the general PSD2 register and the subjekty.nbs.sk database.

why_it_matters: Agent counts are a leading indicator of distribution build-out; if they are only inside the PSD2 JSON, extraction must parse nested agent records rather than expect a list page.

description: No SK register specifically enumerating card acquirers, independent ATM deployers (IAD) or POS terminal operators was found; these activities are not separately licensed and therefore not separately registered.

result.result_summary: Register searches across NBS, EBA and company registers returned no acquirer/ATM-operator-specific list.

why_it_matters: The acquiring and ATM/POS cells cannot be populated from a register alone — they must be assembled by joining licence registers with SK NACE codes in RPO and with NBS payment statistics.

description: ORSR (orsr.sk) exposes no official public API or bulk export; access is via a legacy web search UI only, with third parties (Slovensko.Digital) supplying the API layer.

result.result_summary: Confirmed by the ORSR about page and by the existence of third-party mirror APIs.

why_it_matters: Bulk company-data collection depends on a third-party re-publisher whose terms and continuity are outside our control; a sourcing risk to record.

description: Exact current URLs for Obchodný vestník and for the Štatistický úrad RPO landing page were not confirmed by direct fetch within this pass; the institutions and registers themselves are certain, the paths are hypotheses.

result.result_summary: Search results referenced these registers via portal pages and third-party descriptions rather than the canonical entry URL.

why_it_matters: The deterministic liveness pass should expect redirects here rather than treating a non-200 as a dead source.
